title: Echocardiography deep learning of diastolic dysfunction stratifies aortic stenosis
summary: A previously validated echocardiography deep learning model of diastolic dysfunction was applied to 898 ARIC participants with aortic valve sclerosis. A higher predicted probability was associated with new aortic stenosis (adjusted HR 3.482, 95% CI 2.061-5.884). Validation cohorts were very small (50 patients with mild-to-moderate stenosis and 18 with PET/CT). The model was pre-existing and the study is retrospective; preprint of 2024-05-31.
ai_technology: Previously validated echocardiography-based deep learning model estimating probability of diastolic dysfunction
organization: Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School; Semmelweis University

evidence.tested: Association with outcomes in 898 ARIC participants; two small additional cohorts (n=50 and n=18).
evidence.unknown: Predictive value in larger independent cohorts and peer-reviewed status are not established; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: An existing deep learning model supplied the diastolic dysfunction risk measure analyzed against valve disease progression.
